To summarize, the key findings of our research, stated in one sentence that includes all relevant information, are that
we have demonstrated the acceleration of electrons by a laser beat wave in a plasma.
we have demonstrated the acceleration of electrons by a plasma beatwave in a laser-plasma interaction experiment.
In summary, our research is concerned with
developing a high power, high efficiency laser-plasma accelerator for use in the generation of high energy electrons.
the development of a high gradient, short wavelength, high efficiency accelerator based on the plasma beat wave mechanism.
the acceleration of relativistic electrons in plasma beatwave experiments.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the electron acceleration in a laser beat wave is possible and the energy gain is in the order of 2-3 times the laser energy.
the laser beat wave acceleration of electrons has been demonstrated.
the laser beat wave accelerator has been demonstrated to accelerate electrons from 12 to 22 MeVs.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
we have demonstrated the feasibility of the beat wave acceleration of injected electrons.
a 1-cV/m beat wave acceleration gradient was obtained in an electron plasma density of 10/sup 14/ cm/sup 3/ and 1 GeV m/sup -1/ was obtained in a 10/sup -3/T/sub e/ plasma.
the acceleration of the injected electrons is consistent with the theory of the laser beat wave accelerator.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the electron beam quality is not degraded by the plasma beatwave acceleration.
the electron acceleration in the beatwave accelerator is very robust.
the laser beat wave accelerator can be operated at the resonant plasma density, which is 10/sup 3/ times lower than the previously demonstrated value.
